S-003.objective: T3: Workspace manager — snapshot pinning, per-visit provisioning, resume

findings.summary: backend: container silently falls through to in-process worktree provisioning in provisionWorkspace (manager.ts:345) with no typed error; combined with computeGuarantee it yields a sandbox-labeled in-process session (see F-001/F-006).

Pinning re-resolves the live source on every isolated spawn (production-host.ts:367); resume never re-uses the stored snapshot_pinned commit. Spec §5: 'resume re-uses the stored commit (never re-resolves a moved ref)'; INV-002 requires one immutable run-start pin. A moved ref/HEAD mid-run makes ensureSnapshotCheckout DELETE and recreate the shared pinned checkout, so later visits use a different commit than the record claims.

Confined file tools are rooted at the integration workspace, not the role workspace. computeGuarantee sets projection.workspaceRoot = pinDir (this.cwd) as an un-filled 'placeholder'; resolveMountPath resolves relative mounts to <primary>/<sha8>/<rel> (a path that does not exist — real layout is runStateDir/snapshots/<sha8>). Runtime proof: computeGuarantee for a provisioned role returns workspaceRoot = primary checkout. Result: an isolated role's read/grep/find/ls/edit/write all resolve against and stay inside the INTEGRATION checkout — read-only roles can see the whole primary checkout (AC-002 inverted) and writable workers can write directly into the integration worktree (AC-003 inverted; violates §7.3.5 explicit-integration rule and INV-005's spirit). The provisioned worktree is merely the session cwd.

Delegation children of an ISOLATED parent still derive from the primary checkout (delegation/* untouched): child clean-check + base-commit use the primary repo, so the child sees at least the full primary checkout — wider than the isolated parent's projection. Spec §11 requires the child's primary-checkout base to become the parent's workspace root (INV-007, no privilege escalation via delegation).

StubHost 'parity' only mkdtemps a dir under cwd and passes workspaceRoot = this.cwd; because the stub workspace is inside cwd, the same wrong-root shape as F-001 is unobservable in the stub. session_started.workspace descriptor (core/types.ts) is never populated at runtime; no-op 'void warning' loop and redundant ternary in the workspace_provisioned record.

The entire artifact pipeline is dead code: src/host/artifacts/{collect,route,index}.ts is imported by NO host module (loop.ts/production-host.ts/stub-host.ts), NOT exported from src/index.ts, and referenced by ZERO tests. At runtime: no declared-artifact collection, no auto-patch generation, no artifact_collected/artifact_rejected records, no seed artifacts section — none of §7.2/§7.3 executes. Additional latent bug: collect.ts containment check string-compares the RAW declared (relative) path against absolute projection roots, so every legitimate relative declaration would be rejected 'outside_projection' even if wired. README + CHANGELOG describe the pipeline as functional. T5's task definition required src/host/{production-host,loop}.ts wiring + tests — both absent.

computeGuarantee labels backend: container as 'sandbox' (no writable host mount) while the host runs the role in-process (F-001) — no OS boundary exists in this build (src/host/rpc absent; T8 deferred). Runtime proof: provisionWorkspace(backend:'container') => backend 'worktree' in-process; computeGuarantee(backend:'container') => 'sandbox' with tools incl. bash + shell:container (validator-valid manifest). A session with full host bash is recorded guarantee 'sandbox' — direct INV-006 / AC-006 violation (a stronger guarantee is claimed than exists). Spec's own fallback (§8.3/§19 Q1=no): ship shared/worktree/copy with sandbox documented unavailable — the validator/host must then reject or typed-error a container manifest, never silently downgrade.

acceptance_checks: S-007-A1: AC-001…AC-007 as automated E2E scenarios

findings.summary: E2E 'acceptance' scenarios assert only spawn success. AC-002/AC-003: no canary files, no file-operation attempts (spec §14.6/§17 T7 explicitly require canary-based AC-002/003). AC-005: two role sessions spawned sequentially; spec requires two CONCURRENT read-only DELEGATION children on one shared snapshot. AC-004: no artifact routing (pipeline dead — F-002). AC-006: unit-level computeGuarantee calls only. Consequence: all 1043 tests pass while F-001..F-004 behaviors are broken — the suite cannot observe the wiring defects because no test exercises an isolated role's file tools or artifacts through the real production path.

findings.summary: Docs describe unshipped behavior. README quick-guide presents `container` as an option and the guarantee matrix asserts container→sandbox for a backend that never containerizes in this build (F-006); the artifact pipeline section and the CHANGELOG entry ('collects declared artifacts (plus auto-patches for writable worktrees), and routes them into the next role's workspace') claim functionality that is dead code (F-002). T9 acceptance 'a reader can configure an isolated campaign from the README alone' is not met: following it yields inverted file-tool rooting (F-001) and a no-op artifact channel. The section structure/wording is otherwise solid and must be retained/adjusted in remediation.
Historical reviewer finding F-008 (corrected in this remediation): README and AGENTS.md repo-layout authorities used the obsolete non-archived FSM-spec path.
